title: What is known about 1RB0LA_1RC0RE_0LD0RF_1LA1LD_0RA1RE_---0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_1RC0RE_0LD0RF_1LA1LD_0RA1RE_---0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its run is a sequence of epochs, each starting from one long reservoir of blocks and a short tail. For seven of the eight tails that have turned up, the next epoch is now known for every size (a symbolic run, not yet in Lean). The eighth, S1, starts an epoch that contains a binary counter, and what the counter leaves behind is not understood. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves by the kernel the round-trip rule of the main regime and the 14-trip cycle of the second one for all sizes. A symbolic run of the accelerated simulator gives the epoch map for the tails S0 and S2 to S7 for every reservoir size n ≥ 2000 (28 classes by n mod 4, none halts; checked against the plain simulator, not in Lean). Epochs with the tail S1 run a binary counter with about log2 n digits, and their outcome depends on those digits: no finite set of classes covers them. No halt in the first 4.9·1014 steps (accelerated run).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The main regime, for all sizes
claims.text: Write Q a R for A>(01110)^a 0 1 1 1 1 (001)^a R with blank tape to the left. One round trip of the head takes Q (a+1) (01111 01111 R) to Q (a+2) (01111 R) in 28a + 55 steps, whatever R is; iterated, j round trips eat j blocks of a reservoir (01111)^(k+1+j).

claims.title: The right-end eater, for all sizes
claims.text: Write Z a c d for A>(01110)^a 0 1 1 1 1 (001)^c 1 1 0 0 1 0 0 1 1 1 1 (001)^d 1 1 0 0 1, blank on both sides. Fourteen round trips take Z (a+1) (c+1) (d+9) to Z (a+15) (c+1) (d+5) (224a + 168c + 168d + 4068 steps): a small machine at the right end comes back to the same shape having eaten 4 blocks 001, while the left part gains 14 blocks; iterated in Z_iter.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 50,756 cells have been visited and 28,037 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.538). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.385).

claims.title: The run enters both regimes
claims.text: After 853,764 steps from blank tape the configuration is Q 5 ((01111)^287 T) with T = 0 0 1 1 1 1 0 1 1 1 1 1 0 1 1 1, so 286 round trips follow by the rule above; after 4,090,752 steps it is Z 359 293 278, so 68 periods of the eater follow, to Z 1311 293 6. The bounded runs are evaluated with native_decide; the rest is kernel.

claims.title: C never reads 1 then 0 (so far)
claims.text: The only halting entry is F reading a 0, and F is entered only from C>1 (write 0, move right): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 1 with a 0 to its right. In the first 108 steps F is entered 6,823,520 times, always onto a 1.
claims.where: a transition counter over the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps

claims.title: Big cycles that grow about eightfold
claims.text: From blank tape the regimes come in the order Q with reservoir 292, Q with 296, Z with c = 293 and d from 288 down to 2 (4,090,752 to 22,188,348 steps), a transition, then Q with 2362, Q with 2366, Z with c = 2363 (from 217,524,700 steps, still running at 3·10<sup>8</sup>). Each big cycle multiplies the reservoir by about 8. The transitions (the eater meeting the end of its blocks, the reservoir running out) are not analysed.

claims.title: Epochs: the tape comes back to A> (01111)^n S
claims.text: Along the run from blank tape the left-A records of the form A> (01111)^n S (S at most 60 cells, n ≥ 20) are n = 63, 293, 2363 and 18924, at steps 42,291, 853,349, 54,698,577 and 3,502,378,736. Write E(n, S) for that configuration. Started from E(n, S) on otherwise blank tape, the machine reaches a next epoch E(n', S'). Only six tails S0–S5 have turned up so far, besides a few rarer ones from S1. For S0, S2, S3, S4 and S5, both n' and S' depend only on n mod 4, and n' is affine in n on each class: from S0, n ≡ 1 gives S0 with n' = 8n + 19, and n ≡ 0, 2, 3 give S1 with n' = 8n + 23, 8n + 17 and 8n + 20. From S2, n' = 8n + 54, 52, 53, 50. From S3, S4 and S5 the slope is 9/2. These hold at n = 100–115 and n = 400–407 for every tail, and at n = 20–39 from S0. They predict the run's epochs: 293 ≡ 1 gives E(2363, S0), and 2363 ≡ 3 gives E(18924, S1), which the run reaches at step 3,502,378,736. With the accelerated simulator the run from blank tape goes on to n = 350131 (tail S3, step 1,196,474,995,557), n = 1575589 (S3, step 24,366,344,552,101) and n = 7090149 (S1, step 493,555,240,386,637); these follow the class table below (18924 is an S1 epoch).

claims.title: The epoch map for seven tails, for every size
claims.text: For the tails S0, S2, S3, S4, S5 and the two rarer ones S6 = 0011110111110011110111 and S7 = 0011110111101111001, and every n ≥ 2000, the next epoch is known: 28 classes (tail, n mod 4), each with one symbolic run of the accelerated simulator in which n = r + 4x and x is a free variable. The simulator refuses any step whose outcome would depend on x, so a run that ends at E(k + c x, S') holds for every x. From S0, S2 and S6: n' = 8n + 17 … 54 (c = 32 per 4). From S3, S4, S5 and S7: n' = 9n/2 + d (c = 18 per 4). For S0 to S5 the next tails are exactly those of the table measured earlier at n = 100–115 and 400–407. No class halts, and every class leads to S0, S1, S3 or S4; the tails S2, S5, S6 and S7 arise only from S1. All 28 classes were compared at x = 0 and x = 1 with the plain C simulator: next n, next tail and the step count agree in 56 of 56 runs. This is a result of our own tool, not a Lean theorem.

claims.title: An S1 epoch contains a binary counter
claims.text: From E(n, S1) the reservoir is first turned into a block (110011)^k with k about n/2 (k = 200 for n = 400). Then the right-end eater takes the blocks 110011 one at a time, and between it and the big block (100)^N a binary number appears, written with the words 100 (digit 0) and 11100 (digit 1) after a leading 11100: it goes up by one for every two blocks eaten (observed for n = 400: 1, 10, 11, 100, …, 1100010 after 196 blocks), and each new digit costs the big block one word. When the blocks 110011 are used up the eater takes the number apart digit by digit from the low end (50 round trips for 7 digits at n = 400) and leaves a word to its right that depends on the digits. So the outcome of an S1 epoch depends on the binary digits of about n/4, which explains why it shows no residue pattern.

claims.title: Taking the counter apart is not a finite-state process
claims.text: On tapes of the shape seen just before the blocks 110011 run out, with a random number in place of the counter (200 samples each): the part of the tape right of the remaining digits takes 114 different values for numbers of up to 6 digits, 524 for up to 12 and 1,221 for up to 24, and its longest value grows from 60 to 90 cells. A finite set of classes (the method that proved 1RB0RD_1RC0LF_1LA0LB_---1RE_1LB1RA_0LC0RA) therefore does not cover the S1 epochs; a proof would need an invariant over all digit strings. None of the 600 samples halts.

claims.title: No S1 epoch halts in two sampled ranges
claims.text: From E(n, S1) for every n in 2000–2299 and 5000–5199 (exact accelerated runs): no halt, and each reaches a next epoch, with n' between 11.5n and 22.5n. The next tails seen are S0 to S7 and no others (S3 144 times, S1 106, S2 72, S0 63, S4 46, S5 28, S6 22, S7 19).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. For seven of the eight tails seen, the epoch map is settled for every n ≥ 2000 by symbolic runs, and no class halts. Everything now rests on the S1 epochs. An S1 epoch counts in binary up to about n/4 and then takes the number apart, and the result depends on the digits. A proof that it never halts needs an invariant that holds for every digit string, which is a different kind of argument from a finite set of residue classes. The run from blank tape is in an S1 epoch from step 4.9·1014 (n = 7090149); the S1 epoch before it (n = 18924) ended at E(350131, S3).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RB_1LE0LD_0LB1LD_0RA0LF_---0RE up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RE_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RA0LD_0RD1RE_---0LB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine builds its tape out of 5-cell and 3-cell blocks, in epochs that each begin with one long reservoir and a short tail. For seven of the eight tails seen so far the next epoch is known for every size. The eighth makes the machine count in binary, and what it does with the number afterwards is the open part.

facts.text: Both regular regimes proved for all sizes by the kernel.
No halt in the C simulator.
The epoch map for seven of eight tails, every n ≥ 2000 by n mod 4: n' = 8n + c or 9n/2 + c, none halts.
No halt in the accelerated run; epochs at n = 293, 2363, 18924, 350131, 1575589, 7090149.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only halting entry is F reading a 0. F is entered only from C reading a 1 (C writes 0 and moves right), so the machine halts exactly when C>1 0 occurs: C on a 1 with a 0 to its right. In the first 108 steps that moment comes 6.8 million times and the cell to the right has always been a 1.

sections.heading: The main regime: a reservoir turned into growth
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell at the left end in state A. For long stretches the tape then reads

A round trip of the head runs right over the two repeats (E crossing the 3-cell blocks, D and A coming back), takes the first block 01111 of the reservoir and returns; the left part has gained one block 01110 and the middle one block 001. For example a = 5, b = 287 at step 853,764 becomes a = 6, b = 286 after 167 steps. Lean proves it for every a and every tape behind the reservoir: Q (a+1) (01111 01111 R) becomes Q (a+2) (01111 R) in 28a + 55 steps (Q_step), and by induction j trips eat j blocks (Q_iter). The tape to the right of the reservoir is never looked at.

sections.heading: The eater at the right end
html: The second regime has a little machine at the right end of the tape. The tape reads

and the five cells 1 1 0 0 1 at the end are the eater's resting shape. Each round trip changes its shape (it grows to a dozen cells and shrinks again); after 14 trips it is back, 4 blocks 001 further left, while the left part has grown by 14 blocks. Lean proves the 14-trip cycle for all a, c, d (Z_step, Z_iter). The block (001)^c in the middle is not touched; it is the reservoir of the previous main regime.

The eater does not start in its resting shape: when the regime begins it goes through a few hundred irregular trips first, sometimes even giving a block back, before it falls into the 14-trip cycle. That start-up is only observed.

sections.heading: Big cycles, about eight times bigger each time
html: py/phases.py labels every sample. From blank tape:

• main regime with reservoir b = 1, 6, 7, 62, then 292 (steps 853,349 to 2,042,666) and 296;
  • the eater with c = 293, d = 278 down to 2 (steps 4,090,752 to 22,188,348);
  • a transition of about 30 million steps;
  • main regime with b = 2362 (steps 54,698,577 to 132,769,764) and 2366, then the eater with c = 2363, still running at 3·108 steps.

So each big cycle multiplies the reservoir by about 8 and lasts about 64 times as long. Within a cycle everything is proved; a proof that the machine never halts needs the transitions as rules for all sizes, which is the next step. Whether a transition can go wrong depends on the residues of the sizes (the eater eats 4 blocks per period, so where it stops depends on d mod 4), so the cycle map may be Collatz-like.

The big cycles have clean boundaries. At steps 853,349, 54,698,577 and 3,502,378,736 the tape reads A> (01111)^n S with n = 293, 2363 and 18924: one long reservoir and a tail of 14 to 16 cells. Starting the machine on A> (01111)^n S for many n shows that only six tails occur. For five of them the next such tape depends only on n mod 4, with n multiplied by 8 (or 9/2) plus a constant: from the tail S0 = 0011110111110111, n ≡ 1 mod 4 leads back to S0 with 8n + 19, which is the step from 293 to 2363. The sixth tail, S1 = 00111101111001, reached from 2363 with n = 8·2363 + 20 = 18924, behaves differently. Its cycle carries a second long counter, and where it ends shows no pattern in n. That is where the open part of this machine now sits.

sections.heading: The epoch map, and the binary counter in the way
html: An epoch starts from A> (01111)^n S. Running the accelerated simulator with n = r + 4x and x left as a variable gives the next epoch for all sizes at once (for n ≥ 2000):

fromn ≡ 0n ≡ 1n ≡ 2n ≡ 3 (mod 4)
S0S1, 8n + 23S0, 8n + 19S1, 8n + 17S1, 8n + 20
S2S1, 8n + 54S3, 8n + 52S4, 8n + 53S0, 8n + 50
S3S0, (9n − 2)/2S1, (9n − 3)/2S4, (9n − 2)/2S3, (9n − 1)/2
S4S0, (9n − 4)/2S1, (9n − 5)/2S4, (9n − 4)/2S3, (9n − 3)/2
S5S3, (9n + 8)/2S0, (9n + 7)/2S1, (9n + 6)/2S4, (9n + 7)/2
S6S3, 8n + 42S1, 8n + 38S4, 8n + 43S0, 8n + 40
S7S4, (9n + 18)/2S3, (9n + 19)/2S0, (9n + 18)/2S1, (9n + 17)/2

S6 and S7 are two rarer tails (0011110111110011110111 and 0011110111101111001). None of these 28 classes halts, each was compared with the plain simulator at two sizes, and every one leads to S0, S1, S3 or S4. If S1 were as tame, the machine would be settled. It is not. From S1 the machine first turns the reservoir into about n/2 blocks 110011. Then the eater takes these blocks one by one, and next to it a number grows in binary, with 100 for the digit 0 and 11100 for the digit 1: one step up for every two blocks. At n = 400 it counts to 1100010 (98). When the blocks are gone the eater takes the number apart again, lowest digit first, and what it leaves on the tape depends on every digit.

So the result of an S1 epoch depends on the binary digits of about n/4. In 500 sizes tried (n = 2000–2299 and 5000–5199) no S1 epoch halts and each ends in a new epoch 11.5 to 22.5 times larger, with one of the eight tails. On 600 tapes with random numbers in place of the counter none halts either, but the number of different things the eater leaves behind keeps growing with the number of digits (114, 524, 1,221 for up to 6, 12, 24 digits). A finite list of cases cannot cover that; a proof needs a statement about all digit strings.
From blank tape the epochs are n = 63, 293 (S0), 2363 (S0), 18924 (S1), 350131 (S3), 1575589 (S3) and 7090149 (S1, from step 4.9·1014).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.538). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.385).
After 109 steps the tape spans 50,756 cells (31,957 left of the start, 6,034 right), with a density of 1s of 0.552.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RE_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RA0LD_0RD1RE_---0LB: rename A→D, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state B

summary: Bouncer in epochs A> (01111)^n S. For seven of eight tails the next epoch is known for every n (28 classes mod 4, n' = 8n + c or 9n/2 + c, none halts; symbolic run, not Lean). The tail S1 starts an epoch with a binary counter of about log n digits whose outcome depends on the digits: open.
family: epochs with a reservoir; seven tails settled by classes mod 4, the eighth (S1) runs a binary counter
